chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: King Kolax takes Les Wilcox's book to Los Angeles
summary: Les Wilcox's band music was taken by King Kolax, whose planned Ruth Ellington tour fell through and who was stranded at the Elks.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No, mostly from Indiana, because it was right on the Indiana state line. The Hoosiers -- and while in Chicago, King Kolax, he stole a repertoire from this musician that I told you -- Les Wilcox? I went over and played with him? They didn't have a bass player and they'd take turns feeding me? You recall?

All right, well, Les Wilcox was an epileptic, but very few knew. And he always complained about a toothache, and he would drink gin to ease it. And hold gin in his mouth all night when he wasn't playing the horn. And he wrote music, like, individual parts. He didn't write scores. And he always would ask me to go home with him while they would write, keep him company, you know. And I would go with him, and tell him the truth on myself. We were smoking grass, then.

And he would write so he was exhausted and so I would go home and go to bed. Now, Kolax, who's true name was William Littles, they were supposed to come out here, under a banner of Ruth Ellington. But she decided not to make the trip. So Kolax and the band has already rehearsed and everything, and they had the uniforms and everything and at the last minute, she pulls out.
So he takes Les' music and comes out here to Los Angeles, and played one date at the Elks Auditorium, and they
Well, did Ruth ever front the band? Or was it just a plan to --
No, no, she fronted the band. When and where, I don't know. But she did, I mean, because I've heard her name crop up several times.
That I played with King Kolax out here?
What year that Ruth had -- Ruth's name was around as a band leader.
